steps.content: Rain drips from the man's disheveled hair as he squeezes sideways through the ajar door, clutching a crumpled coat against his chest. The door hinge groans, refusing to budge.
Unbelievable. They're right on your doorstep the second the electric bill's due, but ask them to fix a door, and suddenly they've got a million excuses!
Still grumbling, the man squeezes through the gap. He produces several thick books from the unfurled coat, makes room for them on the desk, then whips out an old gas lamp.
The moment he turns the lamp on, two massive, looming silhouettes stretch across the wall.
Ghosts!!!
With a dull thud, the man crumples to the floor.

steps.speaker: Figure in the Dark
steps.content: Oh my... Perhaps we went a little too far with the prank.
The two silhouettes step forward. One of them reaches out and pokes at Morton's hair, which is as messy as a bird's nest.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Did he actually faint from fright?

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Hmm... I don't think so. More likely from low blood sugar induced by hunger... Could you help me get him onto the couch?
Celine and you haul Professor Morton onto the worn-out couch, then feed him some leftover bread crusts found in the back of the fridge, softened with some warm water.
In the meantime, Celine calls the power company and settles the overdue bill. A little while later, the lights flicker on at last, and the man on the couch stirs slowly back to consciousness.
Celine and you haul Professor Morton onto the worn-out couch, then feed him some leftover bread crusts found in the back of the fridge, softened with some warm water.
In the meantime, Celine calls the power company and settles the overdue bill. A little while later, the lights flicker on at last, and the man on the couch stirs slowly back to consciousness.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: You... you're...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm ${PlayerName}, Chief of the MBCC. This is the Bureau's archivist. Sorry for letting ourselves in. The door was open, and no one answered, so we took the liberty. You must be Professor Morton?
Morton eyes the two of you with quiet suspicion, his gaze shifting back and forth through the cracked lens of his glasses.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: That's right. MBCC... Sure, I've heard of it. Can't say it has much to do with me, though. What brings you here?

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Please excuse our intrusion, Professor Morton. We have some questions regarding Maris Andre, and we were hoping you could enlighten us.
You step forward, cutting off Morton's lingering gaze at Celine, and nudge the plate of toast on the coffee table toward him.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You passed out from low blood sugar just now, so we made you something in the kitchen. Hope you don't mind.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: Hey, don't worry about it. If anything, I should be thanking you. Sorry about that. Must've given you a scare.

Muttering to himself, he pushes up from the couch and reaches into his pocket out of habit, fishing for a cigarette, but the lighter produces nothing more than a spark. He gives up and stuffs another piece of toast crust into his mouth instead.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: Right, you said there was something you wanted to know about Maris?

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Yes. I've been reorganizing some historical records lately, and came across a few inconsistencies. You're one of the leading experts in this field, so I asked Chief to bring me here.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Everyone we asked said you rarely show up to events and don't own a phone, preferring to spend all your time on your research. It took quite a bit of effort to track you down... but now we truly see what a devoted scholar you are.
Morton seems rather pleased with all the flattery. Chuckling, he gestures to the side, and Celine settles onto a stool nearby, producing a notebook and pen with practiced grace.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: According to your book, Maris of Glorie, in the N.F. 50s, the metropoles launched an aid program in DisCity, sponsoring children from reputable families or those who showed academic potential. The true purpose was to train spies for their eventual infiltration into DisCity.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: And yet, Ms. Maris came from the slums and didn't meet the selection criteria at the time. So how exactly was she chosen?
The seasoned academic chuckles, then begins sincerely.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: A historical event must be read in the correct context. To understand that, you have to know DisCity's social climate at the time. The wealthy families were well aware of the metropoles' scheme, so many of them found substitutes for their chosen children. It was entirely plausible that Maris went in someone else's place.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I see. Then, to prove that, shouldn't we also verify exactly who she replaced?

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: You're right. It took me six months of digging before I made any headway. She took the place of a merchant's son, and it was around that time she adopted the surname Andre. All of this will be included in the new edition of Glorie, which is coming out next month.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I see. Thank you for clarifying. My next question concerns a patented technology developed by Ms. Maris during the early stages of Mania detection research, which also earned her the honorary title of...

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: I covered that report in the book. Chapter seven.

You're quite surprised. Morton has a thorough answer ready for every question about Maris. He's also able to defend the flaws in his theories. You can't fathom just how much time and effort must have gone into making the fabricated story seem so impeccable.
There is no doubt he is indeed an exceptional historian.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Yes, the report is quite clear. However, the patent number begins with "RE," indicating it was resubmitted at some point. According to the patent office's records, Ms. Maris's name was not listed on the original submission.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: Consider yourself lucky you're not in academia, young lady. You'd have made a fool of yourself.
Morton leans back into the couch, settling into a more comfortable position.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: Under the guidelines of the time, the "RE" prefix denoted a supplementary submission, not a reapplication.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: Reapplications were subject to a time limit, and supplementary submissions were not. Therefore, regardless of who the initial applicant was, the fact that Maris was a co-applicant on the patent is beyond dispute.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: But... when this application was first filed, Ms. Maris hadn't even been born yet.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: That changes nothing. Maris popularized anti-Mania infrastructure. She was the one who completed the puzzle of modern anti-Mania technology. Her name deserves to be on the patent.
Attributing a predecessor's work to someone born later by manipulating the guidelines... That simply makes no sense.
You furrow your brow, meaning to speak up, when Celine gives a quiet nod.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I see, Professor Morton. Compared to outright fabrication, facts altered by exploiting loopholes are indeed far less noticeable.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: What do you mean?
Celine sets down her pen and paper, then draws a stack of documents from her bag.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Before coming to see you, I did some research on Glorie. It turns out that the birthplace of the famous Maris Andre is surprisingly poorly documented. Luckily, I found the records I needed in several satellite towns a few dozen kilometers away.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Suppose there was a leader who was born in the slums, handpicked by the metropoles, and trained to become a spy. After witnessing the suffering of her homeland, she turned against the metropoles and ultimately led her hometown to become a satellite city of DisCity.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Suppose there was a soldier who, after holding the line against countless disasters, enrolled in university, only to return to the battlefield before graduating... and ultimately gave his life during the Eclipse Operation.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Suppose there was a researcher who treated countless Mania patients with crude equipment, collecting invaluable data and samples. Believing herself no more than an amateur, she donated it all to the authorities free of charge. She later died from prolonged Mania exposure, never living to see her name on the patent.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Professor Morton, as a historian, what future would you say awaited them?
Morton's hands grip the edge of the desk, knuckles whitening. He says nothing.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: You seem hesitant to give an answer, Professor. Then, allow me. Their stories were buried under dust, and many years later, they share one common name... Maris Andre.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: Shut up!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Sit down!
You loom over him, drawing your gun.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Maris Andre is so famous and influential that one wrong move could jeopardize the public image of the city's authorities. That's the only reason you're still sitting comfortably at home having this conversation instead of being dragged away in handcuffs. Are we clear?

You never get the chance to put what you learned during your shooting lessons at the Bureau to use. Morton keeps his eyes fixed on Celine, and it becomes clear that her impeccable manners frighten him far more than the barrel of your gun.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: She was real. Of course she was real! Just look at all the evidence!

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: Because of her, civilian anti-Mania movements have flourished, and donations for DisCity's heroes have been pouring in. Isn't all of that thanks to her?! You two have benefited from this too. So why are you...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So you're admitting this book of yours is just a bunch of lies, then?

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: Lies? You've got to be kidding me! Ninety-nine percent of the events in the book actually happened. I didn't make any of them up!
Morton glares back with bloodshot eyes, like a bull ready to charge.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: It fills in the gaps in DisCity's modern history. Every Disian should read it! Say whatever you want. Ten years, twenty years, even a hundred years from now, this book will remain a cornerstone of historical scholarship!

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: People will never forget what she went through. Her legacy will live on in them. No matter the era, her light will always guide them forward...

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: That's one way to glorify deception, Professor Morton. If your only goal was to pass on "her legacy," why didn't you just write a novel instead? Why should any of us willingly wade through dry, tedious historical facts?

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: You're simply satisfying your selfish intellectual desire.
Celine closes her notebook and looks up.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: You're simply satisfying your selfish intellectual desire.
Celine closes her notebook and looks up.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: You deem ordinary people ignorant, so you use your expertise to exploit that weakness and deceive them. You believe your seemingly noble cause can justify deception, the erasure of truth... all for this so-called "gain."
With his darkest thoughts laid bare so effortlessly, Morton finally seems shaken.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: You... just who are you?!

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Take a closer look, Professor.
Morton finally gets a good look at his interviewer who has been standing behind Chief all along.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Take a closer look, Professor.
Morton finally gets a good look at his interviewer who has been standing behind Chief all along.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Take a closer look, Professor.
Morton finally gets a good look at his interviewer who has been standing behind Chief all along.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Take a closer look, Professor.
Morton finally gets a good look at his interviewer who has been standing behind Chief all along.
Through the thick lenses of his glasses, his wary, suspicious eyes gradually widen, and his fingers begin to tremble. Finally, he recognizes that face.
A deathly silence hangs over the dim room. All that remains is his feeble, mumbling voice.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: After the rerouting in WhiteSands, Glorie fell into decline. Developers complained about the poor soil conditions and kept pushing prices down. The locals received barely any compensation and were on the verge of being forced out of their own homes.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: If Glorie could become something special... If it were more than just another unremarkable little town in WhiteSands, its fate would have been entirely different.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: It was around that time that those people came to me with a photocopied set of handwritten notes...

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: Biographical research is my specialty. I know of countless people like that... It's what I've dedicated my life to studying! So many people are forgotten simply because their stories aren't exciting enough, or because of their flaws. They're too ordinary to be seen as heroes, so no one wants to talk about them!

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: All I needed... was one opportunity to bring Glorie's history to light. People would remember these stories, this town, and those nameless heroes...

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Professor Morton.
She leans forward to steady Morton, who is overwhelmed by emotions and on the verge of collapsing, her voice settling back into its usual calm, gentle tone.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Your book does contain fabricated sections, but as you said, over 90% of it is genuine history. Once properly revised, it will still be a remarkable work. As a fellow historian, my respect for your academic expertise remains unchanged.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I know you've poured every penny into your research, persevering through countless hardships. Your dedication is admirable, and that's why I believe you were simply led astray by temptation.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: We historians are rarely tempted by mere money or fame. The truly dangerous lures are ideas disguised as grand ideals, historical missions, or the pursuit of truth.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Poverty cannot kill our conviction, but arrogance can.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: But what matters is that now we both know it is wrong. Professor Morton, would you be willing to hand over the documents those people gave you? We will follow this lead and pursue those behind it. Once this is all over, these precious records will be preserved, joining the endless river of history.
She's tactfully pointed out Morton's weakness without sounding overly critical of his mistake, and she's now even making an offer he cannot possibly refuse.
For a while, Morton trembles harder under her gentle gaze. At last, deflated, he shuffles to the bookshelf and retrieves a safe.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: Here's the original manuscript. The information in the hidden compartment is all true. If they hadn't shown me those records and made me believe I was Glorie's only hope, I never would have accepted their offer...
He clutches the safe with both hands, as if lifting those sheets of paper has drained every last bit of strength he has.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: Once these documents are in the library... will I still have access to them?

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Rest assured, Professor Morton. I have great respect for your work. When all of this is behind you, if you still wish to pursue the truth, you'd be welcome to join us at the library.
He hands the case over reluctantly, drawing a long breath. And somehow, he seems to stand a little straighter now.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: Thank you, Ms. Celine. It was once my dream to work at the Central Library, but I never quite measured up, so I ended up becoming an independent researcher...

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: I'm grateful for your leniency, but... there are still a few things I should probably disclose to you.
With a calm, resolved expression, he bends down and lifts the cushion of the worn couch. Beneath layers of plastic wrapping, you see stacks of glaring banknotes.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: When they paid me, they marked every bill and filmed the entire transaction. After all, accepting the money would prove that I had become their accomplice.

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: But sitting on it every day was like being burned at the stake. I never dared touch a single bill. Take it. Perhaps it'll give me some leverage when I'm put on trial.
When you come out of Morton's home, the overcast skies that have hung over Eastside for days have finally cleared, and the sun is shining brightly.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I didn't expect you to forgive him so easily.

Celine steps over a glittering puddle on the ground deftly. The wind catches her skirt and veil, as though the two of you have been gently swept into a passing cloud. You hear her voice without seeing her face.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Moore

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Though, today's events remind me of someone I once knew. The response that person gave in the end was quite different from Morton's. Would you like to hear it, Chief?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What did this person say?

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: He said that as long as people's lives improved, he didn't care if his name was erased from the library's records. He believed the welfare of the living was far more important than lifeless knowledge preserved on paper.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...And what became of him?

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: His reputation was utterly ruined. His name was removed from every work he had authored, and he vanished completely from academia. But the people he had helped never forgot him. He remained in history in another form.
She pauses beside you. Perhaps it is the weather, but you could almost swear that detached smile of hers looks genuinely warm and bright for a moment.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Which response do you prefer, Chief?

options: That unnamed figure was indeed brave.
An ordinary person like me doesn't really think about this kind of thing.

choices.text: That unnamed figure was indeed brave.
An ordinary person like me doesn't really think about this kind of thing.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: At its core, history is a collection of objective facts. Its keepers must possess an impartial heart, a commitment to truth, and the resolve to leave an honest account for future generations.
B: That unnamed figure was indeed brave.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: To many, history is no different from mere tales. We look back on history in search of lessons that can guide us toward a better life. So... being able to achieve that goal directly would indeed be a tempting idea.
C: An ordinary person like me doesn't really think about this kind of thing.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Pfft, that's indeed a very "Chief-like" answer. I think I could use a little bit of that frankness myself. That would definitely help me get over some past troubles that still haunt me.
(Convergence)
You can tell she's just giving you a polite answer. Someone as tactful as her would never reveal her true feelings under these circumstances.
Against the fading light of the setting sun, she lifts the photocopy in her hand and holds it out toward you.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Chief, I doubt we can stop the upcoming memorial events for Maris Andre with what we've gathered today alone.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: You may have heard of the Pierce family of Eastside. They built their reputation through collecting and restoring historical artifacts, but after a change in leadership in recent years, they've expanded into commerce. They have strong connections within the city's elite circles.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: This mark here matches their family crest.
Her finger points to a faint imprint in the bottom-right corner of the photocopy. It's a logo composed of several shields.
You recall seeing this family name in the investigation report. In three days, they are hosting a banquet to celebrate the inauguration of the Maris Andre Memorial Hall.
